claim: The molecular bases of heteromeric assembly in epithelial sodium channels (ENaCs) are not fully understood.
source: The molecular bases of heteromeric assembly and link between Na+ self-inhibition and protease-sensitivity in epithelial sodium channels (ENaCs) are not fully understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field, indicating a gap in understanding.

claim: ENaC subunits – α, β, and γ – assemble in a counterclockwise configuration when viewed from outside the cell.
source: Previously, we demonstrated that ENaC subunits – α, β, and γ – assemble in a counterclockwise configuration when viewed from outside the cell with the protease-sensitive GRIP domains in the periphery (Noreng et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The protease-sensitive GRIP domains are located in the periphery of ENaC.
source: Previously, we demonstrated that ENaC subunits – α, β, and γ – assemble in a counterclockwise configuration when viewed from outside the cell with the protease-sensitive GRIP domains in the periphery (Noreng et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The structure of ENaC was resolved by cryo-electron microscopy at 3 Å.
source: Here we describe the structure of ENaC resolved by cryo-electron microscopy at 3 Å.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the resolution of the structure determined in this study.

claim: A combination of precise domain arrangement and complementary hydrogen bonding network defines the subunit arrangement in ENaC.
source: We find that a combination of precise domain arrangement and complementary hydrogen bonding network defines the subunit arrangement.
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The α subunit has a primary functional module consisting of the finger and GRIP domains.
source: Furthermore, we determined that the α subunit has a primary functional module consisting of the finger and GRIP domains.
evidence: This claim is based on structural and functional analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The functional module in the α subunit is bifurcated by the α2 helix dividing two distinct regulatory sites: Na+ and the inhibitory peptide.
source: The module is bifurcated by the α2 helix dividing two distinct regulatory sites: Na+ and the inhibitory peptide.
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Removal of the inhibitory peptide perturbs the Na+ site via the α2 helix.
source: Removal of the inhibitory peptide perturbs the Na+ site via the α2 helix highlighting the critical role of the α2 helix in regulating ENaC function.
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis and inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The α2 helix plays a critical role in regulating ENaC function.

claim: ENaC is expressed apically in specialized epithelial tissues.
source: In the specialized epithelial tissues, the apical expression of the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) gives rise to a transepithelial directional flow of Na+ ions (Palmer and Frindt, 1986).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Apical expression of ENaC gives rise to a transepithelial directional flow of Na+ ions.

claim: ENaC function is crucial in proper regulation of blood volume and pressure.
source: ENaC function is therefore crucial in proper regulation of blood volume and pressure, as well as surface liquid volume in the respiratory and reproductive systems (Boggula et al., 2018; Hummler et al., 1996; Rossier, 2014).

claim: Gain-of-function mutations in ENaC are observed in Liddle syndrome.
source: In humans, the essential role of ENaC in blood volume and pressure regulation is highlighted in gain-of-function mutations, as observed in Liddle syndrome, and also in loss-of-function mutations in pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1, severe genetic diseases that lead to hyper- and hypotension, respectively (Palmer and Alpern, 1998; Liddle and Coppage, 1963; Shimkets et al., 1994; Cheek and Perry, 1958; Hanukoglu, 1991; Strautnieks et al., 1996; Chang et al., 1996; Edelheit et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in ENaC are observed in pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1.

claim: ENaC belongs to the ENaC/degenerin family.
source: ENaC belongs to the ENaC/degenerin family, defined by Na+-selectivity, voltage independence, and amiloride sensitivity (Kellenberger and Schild, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The ENaC/degenerin family is defined by Na+-selectivity, voltage independence, and amiloride sensitivity.

claim: Members of the ENaC/degenerin family have subunits that consist of short intracellular N- and C-termini, two membrane-spanning helices, and a large cysteine-rich extracellular domain (ECD).
source: Members of this family, including the well-studied relative Acid-Sensing Ion Channel (ASIC), have subunits that consist of short intracellular N- and C-termini, two membrane-spanning helices, and a large cysteine-rich extracellular domain (ECD) that can form homo- or heterotrimeric ion channels (Jasti et al., 2007; Noreng et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Members of the ENaC/degenerin family can form homo- or heterotrimeric ion channels.
source: Members of this family, including the well-studied relative Acid-Sensing Ion Channel (ASIC), have subunits that consist of short intracellular N- and C-termini, two membrane-spanning helices, and a large cysteine-rich extracellular domain (ECD) that can form homo- or heterotrimeric ion channels (Jasti et al., 2007; Noreng et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: ENaC subunits α, β, and γ form trimers which are arranged in a counterclockwise direction when viewed from the extracellular space.
source: In the case of ENaC, three homologous subunits, α, β, and γ, form trimers which are arranged in a counterclockwise direction when viewed from the extracellular space (Noreng et al., 2018; Collier and Snyder, 2011; Collier et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Homomeric α ENaC can form functional ion channels.
source: Seminal cloning and functional studies of the ENaC subunits demonstrated that while homomeric α and diheteromeric forms of ENaC containing α/β or α/γ can form functional ion channels, the α-β-γ presents robust Na+ currents indicating that the triheteromeric form is the favored assembly (Canessa et al., 1993; Canessa et al., 1994; Staruschenko et al., 2005; Lingueglia et al., 1993; Firsov et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Diheteromeric forms of ENaC containing α/β can form functional ion channels.
source: Seminal cloning and functional studies of the ENaC subunits demonstrated that while homomeric α and diheteromeric forms of ENaC containing α/β or α/γ can form functional ion channels, the α-β-γ presents robust Na+ currents indicating that the triheteromeric form is the favored assembly (Canessa et al., 1993; Canessa et al., 1994; Staruschenko et al., 2005; Lingueglia et al., 1993; Firsov et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Diheteromeric forms of ENaC containing α/γ can form functional ion channels.
source: Seminal cloning and functional studies of the ENaC subunits demonstrated that while homomeric α and diheteromeric forms of ENaC containing α/β or α/γ can form functional ion channels, the α-β-γ presents robust Na+ currents indicating that the triheteromeric form is the favored assembly (Canessa et al., 1993; Canessa et al., 1994; Staruschenko et al., 2005; Lingueglia et al., 1993; Firsov et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The α-β-γ triheteromeric form of ENaC presents robust Na+ currents.
source: Seminal cloning and functional studies of the ENaC subunits demonstrated that while homomeric α and diheteromeric forms of ENaC containing α/β or α/γ can form functional ion channels, the α-β-γ presents robust Na+ currents indicating that the triheteromeric form is the favored assembly (Canessa et al., 1993; Canessa et al., 1994; Staruschenko et al., 2005; Lingueglia et al., 1993; Firsov et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The triheteromeric form (α-β-γ) is the favored assembly of ENaC.
source: Seminal cloning and functional studies of the ENaC subunits demonstrated that while homomeric α and diheteromeric forms of ENaC containing α/β or α/γ can form functional ion channels, the α-β-γ presents robust Na+ currents indicating that the triheteromeric form is the favored assembly (Canessa et al., 1993; Canessa et al., 1994; Staruschenko et al., 2005; Lingueglia et al., 1993; Firsov et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and inference from the data.

claim: ENaC activity is primarily modulated by proteases that remove peptidyl tracts in the ECD.
source: Unlike other ion channels, ENaC activity is primarily modulated by proteases that remove peptidyl tracts in the ECD (Vallet et al., 1997; Sheng et al., 2006; Kashlan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Removal of polypeptides irreversibly converts ENaC channels from a low-channel-activity state to constitutively active channels.
source: Removal of these polypeptides irreversibly converts ENaC channels from a low-channel-activity state to constitutively active channels (Carattino et al., 2006; Bruns et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The α subunit is cleaved twice by furin.
source: Canonically, the α subunit is cleaved twice by furin, while the γ subunit is cleaved once by furin and once by prostasin (Carattino et al., 2006; Bruns et al., 2007; Hughey et al., 2004; Carattino et al., 2008a; Passero et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The γ subunit is cleaved once by furin and once by prostasin.
source: Canonically, the α subunit is cleaved twice by furin, while the γ subunit is cleaved once by furin and once by prostasin (Carattino et al., 2006; Bruns et al., 2007; Hughey et al., 2004; Carattino et al., 2008a; Passero et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The β subunit does not have canonical protease sites.
source: Of note, the β subunit does not have canonical protease sites.

claim: Extracellular Na+ attenuates ENaC activity by binding to allosteric sites in the ECD.
source: Conversely, extracellular Na+ attenuates ENaC activity by binding to allosteric sites in the ECD, an effect referred to as Na+ self-inhibition (Fuchs et al., 1977; Awayda, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The effect of extracellular Na+ attenuating ENaC activity is referred to as Na+ self-inhibition.
source: Conversely, extracellular Na+ attenuates ENaC activity by binding to allosteric sites in the ECD, an effect referred to as Na+ self-inhibition (Fuchs et al., 1977; Awayda, 2016).

claim: Cleavage of the α subunit abrogates Na+ self-inhibition.

claim: The finger and the specialized GRIP domains are not found in ASIC.

claim: The overall improvement of the map quality reveals for the first time the molecular source of the preferred channel assembly.

claim: ENaCFL comprises wild-type α and β, and N-terminally eGFP-tagged γ.

evidence: This is a description of the constructs used in the study.

claim: ENaCFL behaves like wild-type ENaC as measured by electrophysiology.

claim: Resolution is higher in the channel core, calculated up to 2.6 Å.

claim: Functional ENaC channels require at least one α subunit.
source: It is known that functional ENaC channels require at least one α subunit (Canessa et al., 1994; Fyfe and Canessa, 1998; McNicholas and Canessa, 1997).

claim: All purified ENaCs contain at least one γ subunit because the γ subunit gene contained the purification tag.
source: Additionally, because the γ subunit gene contained the purification tag, all purified ENaCs contain at least one γ subunit (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).

claim: No classes with one or two Fabs forming a 35° and 120° angle about the pseudo three-fold axis were detected.
source: Thus, if other combinations of ENaC heteromers were present, classes with one (α-γ-γ) or two Fabs (α-γ-β or α-α-γ) forming a 35° and 120° angle about the pseudo three-fold axis, respectively, would be observed (Figure 1a; Stewart et al., 2011; Baldin et al., 2020). However, no such classes were detected (Figure 1—figure supplements 2, 3 and 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM data and analysis.

claim: All subunit interfaces share van der Waals interactions between the first two helical turns of the α2 helix and the α6 helix of the adjacent subunit.

claim: The α2 helices are capped by conserved serine residues.
source: Additionally, these α2 helices are capped by conserved serine residues (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).

claim: The α subunit acts as a hydrogen bond donor to the β subunit.
source: Thus, the α subunit acts as a hydrogen bond donor to the β subunit (Figure 1f).

claim: In silico models of homomeric forms of each ENaC subunit were generated using the coordinates of the ENaCFL structure, assuming C3 symmetry around the three-fold axis.

claim: The assumption of C3 symmetry for homomeric models is reasonable based on structures of the closely related ASIC.

claim: Comparison of homomeric models reveals steric clashes in both the distal (finger/knuckle domain interface) and core (lower palm/thumb domain interface) ECD of the β and γ subunits.

claim: The βhomo channel α6 and α2 helices are 3 Å closer than the αhomo channel.

claim: The γhomo channel appears less stable in the distal ECD region, with α6 and α2 clearly intersecting.

claim: The core ECD of the γ- and α subunits are similar.

claim: The β11-β12 linkers of the γ- and α subunits are both similar to that of the ASIC open and closed states.

claim: The β subunit β11-β12 linker resembles that of ASIC trapped in the desensitized state.

claim: None of the steric clashes observed in βhomo and γhomo are obvious in the αhomo channel.
source: None of these steric clashes are obvious in the αhomo channel, as expected given this channel's ability to pass current in vitro.
